subject.title: telegram: isolated-ingress handler-timeout dead-letters a user message silently (no reply, no replay, nothing surfaced)

question: For Telegram isolated-ingress failed tombstones, should OpenClaw preserve terminal dead-letter semantics and add visibility, or should handler-timeout rows be replayed automatically?
rationale: The current terminal tombstone behavior avoids duplicate side effects, but the user-visible and operator-visible recovery contract is a product reliability choice that affects retry policy, status/doctor surfaces, and Telegram user messaging.

options.title: Surface And Notify Failed Tombstones
options.body: Preserve terminal failed rows for unsafe timeout and retry-limit cases, add failed-ingress counts/details to operator surfaces, and send one duplicate-safe failure notice when a user message is dead-lettered.

options.title: Replay Handler-Timeout Tombstones Once
options.body: Allow a guarded one-time replay for handler-timeout rows with zero attempts, but require proof that late original handlers cannot duplicate replies or session effects.

options.title: Operator Visibility Only
options.body: Expose failed tombstones in status or doctor without user notices, accepting that senders may still see silence while operators get a repair path.

recommendation.title: Surface And Notify Failed Tombstones
recommendation.body: Preserve terminal failed rows for unsafe timeout and retry-limit cases, add failed-ingress counts/details to operator surfaces, and send one duplicate-safe failure notice when a user message is dead-lettered.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh authored the major timeout and spooled replay lifecycle fixes that best frame the single-processing versus replay tradeoff.
